$comment: Normative vectors for docs/design/portable-query-payload.md, checked by tests/DotnetInspector.PortableQueries.Tests against src/QuerySpace. encode: intent -> canonical bytes, which must also decode and re-emit unchanged. encode-reject: intent refused before canonicalizing, with reason. reject: bytes refused at decode, with reason. pair: two (queryId, canonical) states and whether they are the same query. Keys, dimensions, and named orders are illustrative.

encode.name: package-query
encode.description: A package query: three terms including the typed prefix, one execution bound, no stages, no order. Scope travels as a term; its value is the typed prefix, not the host spelling with its terminal star.

encode.name: package-query-entered-in-another-order
encode.description: The same query with terms and properties supplied in a different sequence. Identical bytes to package-query: both share one link and one packet state.

encode.name: package-query-with-exact-duplicate
encode.description: An exact duplicate term collapses because conjunction is idempotent; bytes equal package-query. The four parsed terms were still charged against the term limit before collapse.

encode.name: empty-intent-part-is-omitted
encode.description: An intent may carry an empty part; canonical form omits it rather than emitting []. The same bytes arriving on the wire with an empty array are refused, because canonical form never contains one.

encode.name: same-key-terms-break-ties-on-operator-then-value
encode.description: Three terms on one key, supplied scrambled. A key-only sorter would keep caller order; canonical order breaks the tie on operator text, then value text.

encode.name: every-identity-text-carried
encode.description: Every model identity the earlier vectors did not exercise: operators ne and lte, the tail stage, and a lte alongside gte on one key.

encode.name: multibyte-identity-and-value-at-maximum
encode.description: A 32-character key of two-byte scalars is exactly 64 UTF-8 bytes, and a 128-character value of the same is exactly 256. Limits count bytes, not characters; a character-counting host would admit twice as much.

encode.name: term-values-in-scalar-order
encode.description: Two terms on one key and operator whose values are U+10000 and U+E000, supplied UTF-16-first. Scalar order places U+E000 first; a codec comparing values by UTF-16 code units would not.

encode.name: bound-dimensions-in-scalar-order
encode.description: Two bounds whose dimensions are U+10000 and U+E000, supplied UTF-16-first. Scalar order places U+E000 first.

encode.name: ranking-operations-in-ascending-stage-index
encode.description: Two ranking operations supplied stage 1 before stage 0 canonicalize to ascending stage index after base; a codec that only moved base first would preserve the input order.

encode.name: no-unicode-normalization-precomposed
encode.description: A value with the precomposed e-acute (U+00E9). Values are exact tokens; no normalization is applied.

encode.name: no-unicode-normalization-decomposed
encode.description: The same word with e plus combining acute (U+0065 U+0301). A distinct intent from the precomposed form, with distinct bytes; a normalizing codec would collapse them.

encode.name: raw-solidus
encode.description: A solidus is emitted raw; only quote, backslash, and C0 controls are escaped.

encode.name: empty-value
encode.description: An empty string is an admissible value: it is text of admissible length, and the codec never judges what a value says.

encode.name: empty-intent
encode.description: An intent with no parts canonicalizes to the empty object. Whether such a query means anything is the vocabulary's question, not the codec's.

encode.name: order-reference-at-maximum
encode.description: A 64-byte named-order reference and a 64-byte field key: the identity limit applies to order references too.

encode.name: multibyte-payload-near-maximum
encode.description: Twenty-four terms with two-byte values: about 3,000 UTF-8 bytes but far fewer characters. A host counting characters would admit a payload twice this size.

encode.name: bounds-entered-in-another-order
encode.description: Two bounds supplied in the opposite sequence sort by dimension; declaration sequence carries no meaning between independent dimensions.

encode.name: all-four-parts
encode.description: Every part present once, showing property order t, b, s, o and a field-list baseline order.

encode.name: row-query-baseline-and-ranking
encode.description: Rows of at least medium confidence, baseline by name, first twenty, then the five worst by triage. The ranking operation names stage index 1, the top.

encode.name: row-query-reversed-pipeline
encode.description: The same parts with the stage pipeline reversed: a different question, so different bytes whether or not a given input distinguishes the results.

encode.name: order-operations-supplied-out-of-role-order
encode.description: Operations supplied ranking-first canonicalize to base first then ascending stage index; outer sequence carries nothing once each operation names its role.

encode.name: operation-boundary-a
encode.description: Baseline [a asc], ranking [b desc, c asc]. Must not share bytes with operation-boundary-b: each operation array is its own boundary.

encode.name: operation-boundary-b
encode.description: Baseline [a asc, b desc], ranking [c asc]. Same field terms as operation-boundary-a divided differently; different bytes.

encode.name: field-sequence-a
encode.description: A field-list operation ordering by a then b. Field terms compose lexicographically, so their sequence is meaning and is preserved.

encode.name: field-sequence-b
encode.description: The same two field terms, b then a. A different order, so different bytes from field-sequence-a.

encode.name: window-with-open-bounds
encode.description: Window keeps three slots with null for an omitted bound: a gap in place, never a shorter tuple.

encode.name: scalar-order-not-utf16-order
encode.description: Keys U+E000 and U+10000. Scalar (UTF-8 byte) order places U+E000 first; UTF-16 code-unit order would place U+10000 first. The bytes follow scalar order.

encode.name: quotes-backslash-and-short-escapes
encode.description: Quote, backslash, and the five C0 controls with short escapes round-trip in their short forms.

encode.name: c0-control-lowercase-hex
encode.description: A C0 control without a short escape emits as lowercase u00xx, the packet owner's spelling. System.Text.Json's encoders emit uppercase here.

encode.name: raw-scalars-above-ascii
encode.description: U+007F, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, e-acute, and an emoji all emit as raw UTF-8. System.Text.Json's encoders escape every one of these.

encode.name: literal-backslash-u-text
encode.description: A value whose text is the six characters backslash u d 8 0 0. It is ordinary text, escapes its backslash, and is not an unpaired surrogate.

encode.name: joint-maximum
encode.description: The admissible payload with the most JSON values: 24 terms, 8 bounds, seven top stages plus one window, one eight-field baseline plus seven named rankings. 204 values, far under 3 KiB, so here the value count binds before the byte count.
